items.stem: How is Ausable different from other secret agents?
items.answer: Ausable, unlike other secret agents, wwas very fat with an accent of both French and German. Fowler was expecting a smart and active agent having messages slipped into his hand by a dark beauty. Whereas, Ausable received a telephone call making an appointment in his room.

items.stem: “Ausable did not fit any description of a secret agent Fowler had ever read” What do secret agents in books and films look like, in your opinion ? Discuss in groups or in class some stories or movies featuring spies, detective and secret agents, and compare their appearance with that of Ausable in this story. (You many mention characters from fiction in languages other than English. In English fiction you may have come across Sherlock Holmes or Hercule Poirot, or Miss Marple. Have you watched any movies featuring James Bond)?
items.answer: Fowler, the young and romantic writer got disillusioned and disappointed when he failed to find something unusual. Ausable did not fit the description of a secret agent. Ausable was fat, very fat. He spoke French and German passably. Fowler had imagined to see a mysterious figure. The setting in which Fowler met Ausable also disappointed him. In books and films the secret agents are some mysterious character. They are the members of C.B.I. or C.I.D. Interpol, an international organisation has one of the best detectives. We would find them mostly to be very active and smart unlike Ausable. Sherlock Holmes one of the best detectives in fiction leaves the readers shocked.

items.stem: How does Ausable manage to make Max believe that there is a balcony attached to his room ? Look back at his detailed description of it. What makes it a convincin story?
items.answer: Ausable was a clever secret agent. When he entered his room, he found another person from other organisation in his room. Ausable did not lose his calm. He made up a false story. He said that it was the second time, someone had entered his room through the balcony under the window. Max took the story to be true. It becomes a convincing story due to the simplicity and ease with which Ausable behaves. He does not even panic on finding pistol in hand of Max. If Ausable had acted smartly, Max would not have believed him. The story might have turned into a different one.

items.stem: Looking back at the story, when do you think Ausable thought up his plan for getting rid of Max ? Do you think he had worked out his plan in detail right from the beginning ? Or did he make up a plan taking advantage of events as they happened ?
items.answer: Ausable didn’t have the slightest idea that there would be someone in his room. When he entered the room, he blinked his eyes a few times. He got a shock to find Max in his room. Ausable was not handsome, attractive and smart. But being a good spy he did not panic. With his intelligence and presence of mind he was able to find the solution. He collected the facts and planned very fast. He convinced Max that there was a balcony outside the window. He also told that there was police knocking at the door though he knew that it was the waiter knocking. He gave Max no time to think. He did not use strength but mind to overcome the danger. So, it is true to say that nothing was planned. It was by taking the advantage of the situation things were worked out. Talk About It

items.stem: In this story, Ausable shows great ‘presence of mind,’ or the ability to think quickly, and act calmly and wisely, in a situation of danger and surprise. Give examples from your own experience, or narrate a story, which shows someone’s presence of mind.
items.answer: Just like Ausable showed great ‘presence of mind’ or the ability to think quickly and act calmly and wisely in a situation of danger and surprise, we all must stick to our senses and wits and behave in a composed yet clever manner in times of crisis. I too remember having behaved in such a way some months back. While playing in the park one day, one of my friends fell from the swing and was hit hard on his head. He fainted and his head started bleeding. We were five friends playing in the park and there was nobody around us. Everybody was scared and started crying. I sent one of them to that boy’s place to call his parents and rushed to fetch my bag which had a water bottle in it. I sprinkled some water on my friend’s face after which he regained consciousness. By this time, his parents came and they thanked me for acting wisely in such a situation and took him to the doctor timely. My parents were also very impressed with me.

items.stem: Discuss what you would do in the situations described below. Remember that presence of mind comes out of a state of mental preparedness. If you have thought about possible problems or dangers, and about how to act in such situations, you have a better chance of dealing with such situations if they do arise. (i) a small fire starts in your kitchen. (ii) a child starts to choke on a piece of food. (iii) an electrical appliance starts to hiss and gives out sparks. (iv) a bicycle knocks down a pedestrian. (v) it rains continuously for more than twenty four hours. (vi) a member of your family does not return home at the usual or expected time.
items.answer: (i) Fire in a kitchen can make us turn panicky. Infact in kitchen there is a gas cylinder, which can burst any moment. If a small fire starts in our kitchen, the first step should be to close the regulator and try to open the doors and window of the kitchen. In such a situation we should also put off the main switch. If possible try to put sand over the fire. (ii) Food choked in the mouth of a child can be quite risky. Calm and patience are must for any kind of calamity. The child should be asked to keep quiet and his back should be rubbed softly. If need arises a glass of water can be given to drink. The child should be advised that while eating he should not talk. (iii) Electrical fires can be very dangerous. They can not be put off by throwing water. There can cause short circuit and even bring the whole structure down. In case of such fires, the foremost priority should be to put off the main switch. One should never touch any switch with wet hands and always keep your foot covered. (iv) If you are a passer-by and witness a pedestrian being knocked down. In such a situation, some people simply laugh and create fun. But you must act sensibly. Go near the pedestrian. Try to see where he has been hurt. If need arises, take him to the nearby doctor. At least try to give him first-aid. Such a good act will always pay you in later life. If the injury is serious, take him to the hospital and inform his relatives. (v) Continuous rain can also have some unforeseen consequences. The pipes can get choked and cause a kind of danger to the building structure. Call a plumber to get all the pipes checked. The road may form pits and become breeding grounds for mosquitoes. The danger of accident also increases. Try to form a group with friends of your own age. Sort of community participation would be of great help. Insecticides can be sprayed in stagnant water and water should be cleared off the roads. (vi) It is human nature to show worry for our near and dear ones. If a member of our family does not return home at the usual time then first of all we should check at the place where he was expected to go. After knowing about his time of departure, check with his friends and other associates. If no whereabouts are found out report at the nearest Police Station. You may suggest other such situations.

items.stem: One should never judge a book by its cover. Explain with reference to Ausable and how he outwits Max with his presence of mind.
items.answer: Ausable’s character in “The Midnight Visitor” exemplifies the adage “never judge a book by its cover.” Despite his unassuming appearance, Ausable proves to be quick-witted and resourceful, outsmarting Max through his cleverness and presence of mind, which contrasts with his initial impression.

items.stem: Who was Henry? What role did he play in Ausable’s plans.
items.answer: Henry was a waiter at the hotel where Ausable was staying in France. He unknowingly helped Ausable in his plan by knocking at Ausable’s door at the right moment. His persistent knocking helped Ausable in getting rid of the intruder.

items.stem: Discuss, briefly, the reasons owing to which Fowler was interested in meeting Ausable.
items.answer: Fowler was a writer by profession. He wanted to meet Ausable, a secret agent, to learn about his interesting cases and how he solved them. He might be interested to use the information in creating his stories or drama.

items.stem: Ausable was always one step ahead of everyone. Highlight any two instances from “The Midnight Visitor” when this holds true.
items.answer: In the first instance, Ausable guessed rightly what was going on in Fowler’s mind even in their first meeting. Later on, very cleverly he framed a story on the spur of the moment to move Max out of the room by telling him the fake incident of the balcony and the intruder.

items.stem: Henry unintentionally saved Ausable’s life. Briefly comment.
items.answer: Henry had come to serve water in the room. But, Ausable took the benefit of his knocking at the door. He warned Max that it was police and he would be caught soon if he did not jump out of the window. In this way, Ausable was saved by Henry, though, intentionally.

items.stem: Ausable displays an acute sense of awareness of his surroundings. Justify with any two instances from the text.
items.answer: Ausable displayed an acute sense of awareness of his surroundings at two incidence. He was fully aware of his hotel room’s entrance and exit. He confirmed it already that his room did not have an attached balcony. He had calculated well in advance the time for the waiter’s arrival for room service.

items.stem: Why was Ausable confident that Max would never return ?
items.answer: Believing Ausable’s story about the balcony to be true, Max stepped out of the window. Ausable, however, had concocted a very convincing story, and knew that what awaited him was a drop from the sixth floor. Hence, he was confident that Max would never return.

items.stem: How and why did Max come inside Ausable’s room ?
items.answer: Max had come into the room using a pass key. He had come to get the secret report about some new missiles which, he was sure, was with Ausable.

items.stem: How did Ausable kill Max without using a weapon?
items.answer: Ausable was an intelligent spy. When he found Max waiting for him in his room, he made a story of a balcony under his window. He convinced Max about the balcony. And thus, when someone knocked at the door, Max fearing it to be the police, jumped out of the window and died.

items.stem: Why was Ausable angry with the hotel’s management?
items.answer: Ausable pretended to be angry with the hotel’s management to misguide Max. He said that he had complained to the hotel management to block off the balcony extended under the window of his room. They did not act upon and this was the second time in a month an intruder entered his room.

items.stem: Why did Fowler want to meet Ausable? Why was he disillusioned?
items.answer: Fowler was a very young and romantic writer. He wanted to meet Ausable, the secret agent to learn how Ausable tackled with some exciting events. He was disillusioned because he thought Ausable was an unfit secret agent on account of his fat body and American accent.

items.stem: Who was in Ausable’s room? Why had he come there?
items.answer: It was Max who was in Ausable’s room. He was another secret agent. He wanted to grab the important report on a new missile which was supposed to be delivered to Ausable that night.

items.stem: How did Ausable manage to make Max believe that there was a balcony attached to his room?
items.answer: Ausable made up a story very beautifully. He showed disappointment that in spite of his complaint to block off the balcony attached to his room, no action had been taken. He said that it was the second chance in a month that an intruder had entered his room through balcony.

items.stem: What role did the non-existent balcony play in the story “The Midnight Visitor’?
items.answer: The non-existent balcony plays a very important role in the story. It is on this balcony that Max jumps to save himself from being caught by the police but instead ends up being a dead man.

items.stem: What was someone expected to bring to Ausable’s room?
items.answer: Ausable was expecting a very important paper to be delivered to him that night. He told Fowler that many men and women have endangered their lives to obtain that paper. The paper might well affect the course of history someday soon.

items.stem: What did Ausable tell Max about the balcony of his hotel room ?
items.answer: Ausable told Max that another person before him had also entered his room through the balcony sometime back. Ausable said that it was not the balcony of his room but the balcony of the next apartment, that extended under his window now. Because his apartment and the next apartment used to be one unit once.

items.stem: How was Max outwitted by Ausable in the end of the story ‘The Midnight Visitor’ ?
items.answer: Ausable made Max believe that there was a balcony outside the window of his hotel room, when there was none. Ausable also made Max believe that the policemen were knocking at the door. Therefore, Max dropped out to the balcony to avoid the police but died due to the fall, six storeys below.

items.stem: Why did Fowler come to meet Ausable? Was he able to achieve his target?
items.answer: Fowler was a young and romantic writer. He had come to see Ausable to know about the life of a secret agent. Fowler was fascinated by them and thought of them as mysterious and romantic. He was not able to achieve his target as Ausable was a boring man. His physical appearance didn’t match with that of a normal detective.

items.stem: Why did Fowler feel let down when he met Ausable?
items.answer: Fowler felt let down and disappointed to meet Ausable. He had a different picture of a secret agent in his mind. He thought they looked very mysterious and romantic but he found Ausable a very fat and boring man.

items.stem: “Despite his unusual appearance, Ausable’s presence of mind helped him get rid of Max.” Comment with reference to the story ‘The Midnight Visitor’.
items.answer: In “The Midnight Visitor,” Ausable, despite not fitting the stereotypical image of a cunning and physically agile secret agent due to his unusual appearance, showcases his exceptional presence of mind and quick thinking. When confronted by Max, an adversary, in his hotel room, Ausable cleverly invents a story about a non-existent balcony and an imaginary police arrival. His ingenious bluff about the hotel room being under surveillance with the police due to arrive through a fictional balcony convinces Max. This mental agility and the ability to think on his feet enable Ausable to outwit Max, leading to Max’s panicked attempt to escape through the supposed balcony, which results in his downfall. Ausable’s sharp mind, therefore, compensates for his physical appearance, proving that intellect and psychological tactics can be far more effective in espionage than mere physical prowess.

items.stem: Ausable wins over a very critical situation by his sheer presence of mind without using any physical force. Justify giving examples from the text. Or Ausable has the ability to think quickly, act calmly and wisely in a situation of danger and surprise. Do you agree? Support your answer from the story that you have read. Or We need intelligence more than physical strength in a difficult situation. How is it proved true in the story, “The Midnight Visitor”?
items.answer: Ausable wins over a very critical situation by his sheer presence of mind without using any physical force. When Ausable entered the hotel room he found Max Standing with a pistol aimed at him. Ausable showed no nervousness and sat in an armchair. He used his presence of mind and made up a story at once. He made Max believe that there was a balcony attached to his room. When there was a knock at door, Ausable took no time to announce that it was police to provide him extra protection as he was expecting an important paper. Max feared to be caught and to save his life he jumped through the window and met his end. Ausable’s ability to think quickly, act calmly and wisely in a situation of danger and surprise gets him through unharmed.

items.stem: Ausable knew Fowler was very disappointed on seeing him. What did Ausable say to him and how did he console him? Or What impression do you form of Ausable as a secret agent after reading story “The Midnight Visitor”? Or Ausable did not fit any description of a secret agent Fowler had ever read.” Elaborate, Justify from text?
items.answer: Ausable knew that Fowler was pretty disappointed on seeing him. Fowler had been told that he was to meet a secret agent, a spy, dealing in espionage and danger. He had wished to meet Ausable because Fowler was a young and romantic writer who imagined a secret agent to be associated with mysterious figures in the night, the crack of pistols and drugs in the wine. Instead, Fowler had to spend a dull evening in a French music hall with a sloppy fat man who, instead of having messages slipped into his hand by dark-eyed beauties, got only an ordinary telephone call making an appointment in his room. Though Ausable’s appearance did not match that of a secret agent and he did not really fit the description of one, he was indeed a very intelligent and smart agent. Ausable understood Fowler’s disillusionment and told him to take cheer because he would presently see an important paper for which several people had risked their lives and that could well affect the course of history.

items.stem: How did Ausable use ‘the knock’ at the door in his favour? What light does this throw on his character?
items.answer: There was a sudden knock at the door. Ausable knew it that the water had come to serve the drink ordered by him. He used his presence of mind and informed Max that it would be the police. Even in the most difficult situation when a man was standing aiming a pistol at him, he did not lose his nerves. He said that he demanded extra police protection and asked them to check on him regularly so nothing went wrong with him. He said that the room was unlocked and the police would not hesitate to shoot Max. Max unwittingly jumped outside the room and .got injured. Thus Ausable with his sheer intelligence got through an unimaginable difficult situation.

items.stem: How did Ausable get rid of Max? Or How did Ausable fool Max and get rid of him?
items.answer: Ausable got rid of Max by using his intelligence, alertness and presence of mind. Max met his end by jumping out of a window, which Ausable said had a balcony outside, but there was no balcony and Max dropped down dead. Max’s own foolishness makes him an easy prey to Ausable’s clever thinking. When there was a knock on the door, Ausable told Max it was the police who had come to check on him. Max was convinced and in a bid to escape jumped out of the window without thinking.

items.stem: Give a brief character sketch of Fowler ? What are the values reflected in his character ?
items.answer: Fowler is a young romantic writer, who loves reading mysterious stories. He has a fantasy to meet a secret agent or to see mysterious figures in the night, the crack of guns, drugs in wine, etc. He is not much interested in meeting dull people. He gets easily bored and disappointed. Though he is a writer, he is very timid by heart. He easily loses his cool and gets nervous. The moment he enters Ausable’s room and his eyes meet Max with an automatic pistol in his hand, he is thrilled. He is scared, the moment he realises that it is a waiter and not the police who has knocked at the door. He wants to know about the man in the balcony. He has a horrible experience with Ausable tackling risky situations so calmly.

items.stem: How did Ausable get rid of Max ? Would you call the act of Ausable a violent act ? Do you support violence in prevention of crime ?
items.answer: Max was in Ausable’s room with a pistol in his hand. When there was a knock at the door Ausable convinced Max that it was police. He excited him to hide himself on the non-existent balcony. Max, in terror, jumped from the sixth floor and met his end. No, it cannot be called nonviolence. Ausable saved himself but led Max to death. He made him jump from the eight floor. He concocted the story of a non-existent balcony and convinced him to hide there. He trusted him and jumped to death. Violence should never be supported but in prevention of crime it is inevitable. We cannot tackle the criminals without the use of weapons and violence is inevitable.

items.stem: Suppose you are Fowler. Write a diary entry about your first impression of Ausable after meeting him in a French music hall.
items.answer: Wednesday May, 20xx 10:50 p.m. Dear Diary, Being a young and romantic writer, I have read many books depicting the heroic deeds of secret agents. I have always imagined them to be romantic, mysterious, smart and dashing people. So, I was thrilled when I got a telephonic appointment with Ausable, a very famous secret agent. He told me to meet him at a French music hall in the evening. I was happy because I was going to meet a renowned mysterious figure. But later, I was disappointed to see an extremely fat man wearing casual clothes. This secret agent spoke French and German passably with a slight American accent. In fact, the more time I spent in his company, the more I got bored and disillusioned. He lived in an ordinary hotel and used an ordinary telephone for the purpose of communication, nothing like the life I had imagined for a secret agent. I am disillusioned. Waiting for some action. In disappointment. Fowler

items.stem: Why was Fowler “disillusioned” and why did Ausable tell him to “take cheer” ?
items.answer: Fowler was a young and romantic writer. He thought that the secret agents were mysterious figures who lived adventurous lives. Therefore, he was very eager and keen to meet Ausable. But he found Ausable to be an extremely fat man who lived in a mediocre French hotel and used an ordinary telephone to communicate with others. After passing a dull evening with Ausable in a French music hall, Fowler got bored and disillusioned. But Ausable told Fowler `to take cheer’ or to be happy because in his hotel room he would show Fowler a very important paper. He further told Fowler that several men and women had risked their lives to get that paper and that some day in the near future, that paper might as well affect the course of history.

items.stem: How did Max meet his end? Do you sympathise with him? Why? Why not? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Max jumped through the window to escape from the police, he thought there was a balcony. But he fell down and met his end. We do sympathise with him because he was too easily fooled by Ausable. Even he was armed but he could not outwit Ausable. Max was gullible and Ausable easily made him believe that there was a balcony attached to his room. When there was a kAusable was a successful secret agent. What qualities can be attributed to him? Give some examples.

items.stem: Read the extract given below and answer the questions that follow: Ausable did not fit any description of a secret agent Fowler had ever read. Following him down the musty corridor of the gloomy French hotel where Ausable had a room, Fowler felt let down. It was a small room, on the sixth and top floor, and scarcely a setting for a romantic adventure. Ausable was, for one thing, fat. Very fat. And then there was his accent. Though he spoke French and German passably, he had never altogether lost the American accent he had brought to Paris from Boston twenty years ago. “You are disappointed,” Ausable said wheezily over his shoulder. “You were told that I was a secret agent, a spy, dealing in espionage and danger. You wished to meet me because you are a writer, young and romantic. You envisioned mysterious figures in the night, the crack of pistols, drugs in the wine.” i.
